laws.title: Illegal Weapons Possession
laws.subtitle: Owning firearms without registration or permit
laws.fullDescription: Kazakhstan law requires all civilian firearms to be registered with the Ministry of Internal Affairs. Possessing unregistered weapons, modified firearms, or prohibited weapons such as automatic rifles is a serious criminal offense.
laws.penalty: Up to 7 years imprisonment; forfeiture of weapons
exceptions: Military personnel on duty
Licensed hunters and sports shooters with valid permits

quiz.q: Which agency registers civilian firearms in Kazakhstan?
quiz.explanation: Civilian firearms in Kazakhstan must be registered with the Ministry of Internal Affairs.

laws.title: Illegal Nuclear Material Handling
laws.subtitle: Unauthorized possession or transfer of radioactive substances
laws.fullDescription: Kazakhstan, as a major uranium producer, has strict laws governing radioactive and nuclear materials. Unauthorized handling, possession, transportation, or transfer of nuclear materials is a serious criminal offense that poses catastrophic safety and security risks.
laws.penalty: 5 to 15 years imprisonment
exceptions: Licensed nuclear industry personnel under strict regulatory oversight
laws.sourceLabel: Kazakhstan Law on Atomic Energy Use

quiz.q: Why does Kazakhstan have particularly strict nuclear material laws?
options: It is a major uranium producer
It hosts a nuclear power plant
quiz.explanation: Kazakhstan is one of the world largest uranium producers, making strict nuclear material controls especially important.

laws.title: Drug Trafficking
laws.subtitle: Importing, exporting, or distributing narcotics
laws.fullDescription: Kazakhstan criminalizes the trafficking of narcotic drugs and psychotropic substances at all stages — production, import, export, sale, and distribution. Given Kazakhstan position on major trafficking routes, enforcement is a priority.
laws.penalty: 10 to 20 years imprisonment for large-scale trafficking
exceptions: Licensed pharmaceutical companies
Prescribed medical use

quiz.q: What makes drug trafficking particularly serious in Kazakhstan context?
quiz.explanation: Kazakhstan strategic position on major drug trafficking routes makes narcotics enforcement a national security priority.

laws.title: Tax Evasion
laws.subtitle: Concealing income or assets to avoid tax obligations
laws.fullDescription: Kazakhstan tax law requires individuals and businesses to accurately report all taxable income and pay applicable taxes. Deliberate concealment of income, false deductions, or other fraudulent tax practices constitute criminal tax evasion.
laws.penalty: Fine of up to 2,000 MCI; up to 4 years imprisonment for large-scale evasion
exceptions: Legitimate tax deductions and exemptions provided by law

quiz.q: What does MCI stand for in Kazakhstan penalty calculations?
quiz.explanation: MCI (Monthly Calculation Index) is Kazakhstan standard unit for calculating administrative and criminal fines.

laws.title: Unauthorized Public Gatherings
laws.subtitle: Organizing protests or assemblies without prior notification
laws.fullDescription: Kazakhstan law requires organizers of public gatherings, demonstrations, and pickets to notify local authorities in advance. Organizing unsanctioned mass events can result in fines and administrative detention. Regulations have been updated to allow notification rather than prior permission for most events.
laws.penalty: Fine of 20 to 40 MCI; up to 15 days administrative arrest
exceptions: Spontaneous gatherings in response to immediate events
Cultural and religious celebrations with official status

quiz.q: What changed in Kazakhstan law on public gatherings in recent reforms?
options: Prior permission replaced by prior notification
Only political parties may organize gatherings
quiz.explanation: Kazakhstan reformed its assembly law to require advance notification rather than prior permission for most public gatherings.

laws.title: Computer System Hacking
laws.subtitle: Unauthorized access to protected computer systems
laws.fullDescription: Kazakhstan criminal law prohibits unauthorized access to computer systems, networks, and data. This includes bypassing security measures, installing malicious software, and exploiting vulnerabilities without authorization.
laws.penalty: Up to 3 years imprisonment; up to 7 years if critical infrastructure targeted
exceptions: Authorized security testing by certified professionals with written permission

quiz.q: What increases the penalty for hacking in Kazakhstan?
quiz.explanation: Targeting critical infrastructure systems increases the hacking penalty to up to 7 years imprisonment in Kazakhstan.

laws.title: Money Laundering
laws.subtitle: Concealing proceeds of criminal activity
laws.fullDescription: Kazakhstan anti-money laundering law prohibits converting, transferring, or concealing proceeds of criminal activity to disguise their illegal origin. Financial institutions must implement AML programs and report suspicious transactions to the Financial Monitoring Agency.
laws.penalty: Up to 7 years imprisonment; confiscation of laundered assets
exceptions: None — knowing participation in money laundering is always criminal
laws.sourceLabel: Kazakhstan Law on Countering Legalization of Criminal Proceeds

quiz.q: Which Kazakhstan body oversees anti-money laundering compliance?
quiz.explanation: The Financial Monitoring Agency oversees AML compliance and receives suspicious transaction reports in Kazakhstan.

laws.title: Unsafe Working Conditions
laws.subtitle: Failing to provide required workplace safety standards
laws.fullDescription: Kazakhstan labor law imposes strict occupational health and safety requirements on employers. Workplaces must meet established safety standards, provide necessary protective equipment, and ensure regular safety training. Violations that cause harm to workers result in serious penalties.
laws.penalty: Fine of 100 to 200 MCI; suspension of operations; criminal charges if injury or death occurs
exceptions: Self-employed individuals working alone on their own property

quiz.q: What happens when unsafe working conditions cause worker deaths in Kazakhstan?
quiz.explanation: When unsafe working conditions cause injury or death, criminal charges may be brought against responsible employers.

laws.title: Illegal Caspian Sea Pollution
laws.subtitle: Discharging pollutants into the Caspian Sea
laws.fullDescription: Kazakhstan Caspian Sea coast requires special protection. Discharging oil, chemicals, sewage, or other pollutants into the Caspian Sea or its coastal zones violates both national environmental law and international agreements on Caspian Sea environmental protection.
laws.penalty: Fine of up to 5,000 MCI; criminal charges for large-scale pollution
exceptions: Emergency discharge with immediate reporting and remediation efforts

quiz.q: What international dimension makes Caspian Sea pollution particularly serious in Kazakhstan?
quiz.explanation: Kazakhstan Caspian Sea pollution laws are reinforced by international agreements among all Caspian Sea states.

laws.title: Corruption and Bribery
laws.subtitle: Giving or receiving bribes in public service
laws.fullDescription: Kazakhstan has strengthened its anti-corruption laws significantly. Both giving and receiving bribes constitute serious criminal offenses. Public officials who solicit or accept bribes, and individuals who offer them, face severe penalties. Kazakhstan anti-corruption agency actively investigates such cases.
laws.penalty: Up to 12 years imprisonment; confiscation of property; lifetime ban from public service
exceptions: None — bribery is always criminal regardless of amount

quiz.q: What happens to public officials convicted of bribery in Kazakhstan?
options: They may be rehired after serving time
They face a lifetime ban from public service
quiz.explanation: Beyond imprisonment, Kazakhstani public officials convicted of bribery face a lifetime ban from public service positions.

laws.title: Overstaying Visa
laws.subtitle: Remaining in Kazakhstan beyond authorized period
laws.fullDescription: Foreign nationals in Kazakhstan must depart or regularize their status before their visa or authorized stay period expires. Overstaying without authorization violates immigration law and can result in fines, deportation, and future entry bans.
laws.penalty: Fine; deportation; entry ban of 1 to 5 years
exceptions: Force majeure situations such as medical emergencies documented officially

quiz.q: What can happen to foreign nationals who overstay their visa in Kazakhstan?
quiz.explanation: Overstaying a visa in Kazakhstan can result in fines, deportation, and bans on future entry lasting 1 to 5 years.

laws.title: Extremism and Terrorism
laws.subtitle: Participating in or promoting extremist organizations
laws.fullDescription: Kazakhstan law prohibits participation in, financing, or promoting extremist and terrorist organizations. The law is broadly applied and has been used to address both genuine security threats and, controversially, some religious groups and political dissidents.
laws.penalty: 5 to 20 years imprisonment
exceptions: Legitimate religious practice by non-banned organizations
Academic study of extremism

quiz.q: What type of activity is prohibited under Kazakhstan anti-extremism law?
quiz.explanation: Kazakhstan anti-extremism law targets participation in, financing, and promotion of designated extremist organizations.

laws.title: Illegal Land Use Changes
laws.subtitle: Converting agricultural land without authorization
laws.fullDescription: Kazakhstan maintains strict controls on agricultural land use. Converting agricultural land to other purposes — such as construction or industrial use — without authorization from relevant authorities is prohibited to protect the country food security.
laws.penalty: Fine of 50 to 200 MCI; mandatory land restoration
exceptions: State-approved infrastructure projects with compensation to landholders

quiz.q: Why does Kazakhstan strictly control agricultural land conversion?
quiz.explanation: Kazakhstan controls agricultural land conversion to protect the country food security and maintain productive farmland.

laws.title: Illegal Drug Prescription
laws.subtitle: Prescribing controlled substances without medical justification
laws.fullDescription: Kazakhstan medical law requires that controlled substances be prescribed only when medically necessary and in accordance with established clinical guidelines. Prescribing controlled drugs without justification or for personal benefit is a serious professional and criminal offense.
laws.penalty: Medical license revocation; up to 5 years imprisonment
exceptions: Legitimate palliative care prescriptions within clinical guidelines

quiz.q: What professional consequence faces doctors who illegally prescribe controlled substances in Kazakhstan?
quiz.explanation: Doctors in Kazakhstan who illegally prescribe controlled substances face medical license revocation in addition to criminal charges.

laws.title: Spreading False Information
laws.subtitle: Publishing deliberately false news that disrupts public order
laws.fullDescription: Kazakhstan law prohibits the deliberate dissemination of false information that could cause public panic, undermine state institutions, or disrupt social order. This law has been applied both to address genuine misinformation and, critics argue, to restrict independent reporting.
laws.penalty: Fine; up to 3 years imprisonment
exceptions: Satire and clearly labeled opinion pieces
Good-faith reporting with subsequent correction

quiz.q: What is the intent requirement for criminal false information in Kazakhstan?
options: The information must be deliberately false
quiz.explanation: Kazakhstan law targets deliberately false information, not honest mistakes. Intent to deceive or cause harm is required.

laws.title: Fraudulent Real Estate Transactions
laws.subtitle: Selling or mortgaging property one does not own
laws.fullDescription: Kazakhstan civil and criminal law prohibits fraudulent real estate transactions, including selling properties that are not legitimately owned, double-selling the same property to multiple buyers, and mortgaging property without disclosing existing liens.
laws.penalty: Fine; 3 to 7 years imprisonment for organized real estate fraud
exceptions: Good-faith mistakes with prompt remediation

quiz.q: What is double-selling in the context of real estate fraud?
options: Selling the same property to two different buyers
quiz.explanation: Double-selling — selling the same property to multiple buyers — is a serious fraud offense in Kazakhstan real estate law.

laws.title: Human Trafficking
laws.subtitle: Recruiting or transporting people for exploitation
laws.fullDescription: Kazakhstan criminal law prohibits all forms of human trafficking, including recruitment, transportation, and harboring of people for forced labor, sexual exploitation, or other forms of abuse. Kazakhstan is both a source and transit country for trafficking.
laws.penalty: 5 to 15 years imprisonment; up to 20 years for organized trafficking
exceptions: None — human trafficking is always criminal

quiz.q: What is Kazakhstan role in regional human trafficking?
quiz.explanation: Kazakhstan is both a source and transit country for human trafficking, making enforcement particularly challenging.

laws.title: Pyramid Scheme Operation
laws.subtitle: Running investment schemes based on recruitment rather than returns
laws.fullDescription: Kazakhstan financial law prohibits pyramid schemes — investment arrangements where returns depend primarily on recruiting new participants rather than genuine business activity. Such schemes inevitably collapse, causing widespread financial harm.
laws.penalty: Fine of up to 5,000 MCI; up to 7 years imprisonment for organizers
exceptions: None — all pyramid schemes are illegal regardless of claimed purpose

quiz.q: What distinguishes a pyramid scheme from a legitimate investment?
options: Returns depend on recruitment rather than business activity
quiz.explanation: Pyramid schemes generate returns through recruitment of new members rather than genuine business activity, which is their defining illegal characteristic.

laws.title: Illegal Fishing in Protected Areas
laws.subtitle: Fishing in reserves or using prohibited methods
laws.fullDescription: Kazakhstan has designated numerous protected water bodies and fishing zones. Fishing in these protected areas, using prohibited methods such as electric fishing or dynamite, or exceeding catch quotas is a violation of environmental law.
laws.penalty: Fine of 10 to 100 MCI; confiscation of equipment and catch
exceptions: Scientific research fishing with proper permits

quiz.q: Which fishing method is specifically prohibited in Kazakhstan?
quiz.explanation: Electric fishing is prohibited in Kazakhstan as it is destructive to aquatic ecosystems and kills indiscriminately.

laws.title: Defamation of Public Officials
laws.subtitle: Publishing false statements damaging officials reputations
laws.fullDescription: Kazakhstan law includes provisions protecting public officials from deliberate defamation. While criticized by press freedom advocates, this law distinguishes between good-faith criticism of public figures and the knowing publication of false and damaging statements.
laws.penalty: Fine; up to 2 years imprisonment for criminal defamation
exceptions: True statements
Opinions and commentary clearly presented as such
Public interest journalism

quiz.q: What is the key distinction between protected speech and criminal defamation in Kazakhstan?
options: Defamation requires knowing publication of false facts
Any criticism of officials is criminal
Only TV broadcasts can be defamatory
quiz.explanation: Criminal defamation in Kazakhstan requires knowing publication of false facts, not mere criticism or opinion.

laws.title: Child Sexual Abuse
laws.subtitle: Sexual exploitation or abuse of minors
laws.fullDescription: Kazakhstan criminal law harshly punishes all forms of sexual abuse of children under 16 years of age. This includes contact offenses, production of child sexual abuse material, and grooming. Kazakhstan has strengthened penalties following public concern about child safety.
laws.penalty: 8 to 20 years imprisonment; lifetime supervision for repeat offenders
exceptions: None — any sexual contact with minors is criminal

quiz.q: What additional measure applies to repeat child sexual offenders in Kazakhstan?
quiz.explanation: Repeat child sexual offenders in Kazakhstan face lifetime post-release supervision in addition to lengthy imprisonment.

laws.title: Driving Without a License
laws.subtitle: Operating a motor vehicle without valid driving credentials
laws.fullDescription: Kazakhstan road traffic law requires all motor vehicle operators to hold a valid driving license appropriate to the vehicle category. Driving without a license, or with an expired or suspended license, is a violation subject to fines and vehicle impoundment.
laws.penalty: Fine of 10 to 30 MCI; vehicle impoundment
exceptions: Private land where public traffic laws do not apply
Emergency situations

quiz.q: What happens to a vehicle if the driver is caught driving without a license in Kazakhstan?
quiz.explanation: In Kazakhstan, vehicles driven by unlicensed drivers are impounded, in addition to fines being imposed on the driver.

laws.title: Unauthorized Archaeological Excavation
laws.subtitle: Digging at historical sites without permits
laws.fullDescription: Kazakhstan has a rich archaeological heritage from the ancient Silk Road civilizations. Unauthorized excavation at protected archaeological sites is prohibited to preserve historical artifacts and cultural heritage for scientific study and national identity.
laws.penalty: Fine of 50 to 200 MCI; imprisonment if artifacts removed
exceptions: Licensed archaeologists from accredited institutions with proper permits

quiz.q: Why is archaeological heritage particularly significant in Kazakhstan?
options: It was a center of Silk Road civilizations
It has the world oldest pyramids
quiz.explanation: Kazakhstan Silk Road heritage includes ancient civilizations, making unauthorized excavation a serious threat to irreplaceable cultural history.

laws.title: Unauthorized GMO Cultivation
laws.subtitle: Growing genetically modified crops without approval
laws.fullDescription: Kazakhstan regulates the cultivation and circulation of genetically modified organisms. Unauthorized cultivation of GMO crops without state registration and safety assessment is prohibited, as is import of unregistered GMO seeds.
laws.penalty: Fine of 20 to 100 MCI; destruction of crops
exceptions: Scientific field trials with proper permits from authorized bodies

quiz.q: What must GMO crops undergo before they can be cultivated in Kazakhstan?
quiz.explanation: GMO crops require state registration and safety assessment before they can be legally cultivated in Kazakhstan.

laws.title: Espionage
laws.subtitle: Collecting and transferring state secrets to foreign powers
laws.fullDescription: Kazakhstan criminal law treats espionage as a serious crime against state security. Collecting, storing, or transmitting state secrets — including military, intelligence, economic, or technological information — to foreign states or organizations is strictly prohibited.
laws.penalty: 10 to 20 years imprisonment
exceptions: Authorized intelligence sharing under bilateral agreements

quiz.q: What types of information are considered state secrets in Kazakhstan?
options: Military, intelligence, economic, and technological information
quiz.explanation: Kazakhstan state secrets encompass military, intelligence, economic, and technological information — a broad category.

laws.title: Deliberate Disease Spreading
laws.subtitle: Intentionally infecting others with dangerous diseases
laws.fullDescription: Kazakhstan criminal law prohibits deliberately infecting others with dangerous infectious diseases, including HIV/AIDS and other serious pathogens. Even reckless behavior that results in disease transmission can be criminal if the accused knew of their infection.
laws.penalty: Up to 8 years imprisonment
exceptions: Medical procedures with proper informed consent
laws.sourceLabel: Kazakhstan Criminal Code — Public Health Crimes

quiz.q: Does Kazakhstan law address reckless disease transmission as well as deliberate?
options: No — only deliberate acts are criminal
Yes — reckless transmission by someone who knew of their infection can be criminal
Only transmission to children is criminal
quiz.explanation: Kazakhstan law can cover reckless as well as deliberate disease transmission if the person knew of their infection.

laws.title: Child Labor
laws.subtitle: Employing children in prohibited or hazardous work
laws.fullDescription: Kazakhstan labor law sets the minimum working age at 16 years, with 14–15 year-olds permitted limited light work with parental consent. Employing children under 14, or using children in hazardous conditions, is strictly prohibited.
laws.penalty: Fine of 100 to 300 MCI; suspension of business operations
exceptions: Light work by 14-15 year olds with parental and authority consent
Artistic and cultural performances by minors under supervision
laws.sourceLabel: Kazakhstan Labor Code — Child Labor Provisions

quiz.q: What is the minimum working age in Kazakhstan?
quiz.explanation: Kazakhstan sets the minimum working age at 16, with limited exceptions for light work by 14-15 year-olds with consent.

laws.title: Music and Film Piracy
laws.subtitle: Distributing copyrighted content without authorization
laws.fullDescription: Kazakhstan intellectual property law protects music, film, and other creative works from unauthorized reproduction and distribution. Commercial piracy — selling or distributing counterfeit media — is a criminal offense, while widespread digital piracy is addressed through civil measures.
laws.penalty: Fine; up to 3 years imprisonment for commercial piracy
exceptions: Private personal use of legally obtained content
Educational fair use within prescribed limits
laws.sourceLabel: Kazakhstan Law on Copyright and Related Rights

quiz.q: How does Kazakhstan law treat commercial piracy differently from personal copying?
options: Commercial piracy carries criminal penalties while personal copying is civil
quiz.explanation: Commercial piracy in Kazakhstan is a criminal offense, while personal copying is generally handled through civil measures.

laws.title: Selling Counterfeit Electronics
laws.subtitle: Distributing fake or non-compliant electronic devices
laws.fullDescription: Kazakhstan consumer protection law prohibits the sale of counterfeit electronic devices or devices that do not comply with mandatory technical standards. Fake electronics can be dangerous due to fire hazards, electrical faults, and radiation non-compliance.
laws.penalty: Fine of 100 to 500 MCI; seizure of goods
exceptions: Clearly labeled refurbished or gray-market items with full disclosure
laws.sourceLabel: Kazakhstan Law on Consumer Rights Protection

quiz.q: Why are counterfeit electronics particularly dangerous?
options: They can cause fires and electrical hazards
They void warranties on other devices
quiz.explanation: Counterfeit electronics often lack safety features, creating fire hazards, electrical faults, and radiation compliance risks.

laws.title: Illegal Explosive Possession
laws.subtitle: Owning or storing explosives without authorization
laws.fullDescription: Kazakhstan law strictly controls civilian possession of explosives, detonators, and pyrotechnic substances. Only licensed entities such as mining companies, demolition firms, and military contractors may legally possess these materials under strict regulatory oversight.
laws.penalty: Up to 7 years imprisonment
exceptions: Licensed mining, demolition, and pyrotechnic companies with valid permits
laws.sourceLabel: Kazakhstan Law on Weapons — Explosives Provisions

quiz.q: Which types of entities can legally possess explosives in Kazakhstan?
options: Licensed mining, demolition, and pyrotechnic firms
quiz.explanation: Only licensed mining companies, demolition firms, and pyrotechnic companies may legally possess explosives in Kazakhstan.

laws.title: Illegal Logging
laws.subtitle: Cutting timber in protected forests without permits
laws.fullDescription: Kazakhstan has significant forest protection laws, especially for saxaul forests in the Aral Sea region and montane forests in eastern and southern Kazakhstan. Illegal logging destroys biodiversity, accelerates desertification, and reduces carbon sequestration.
laws.penalty: Fine of 50 to 500 MCI; mandatory reforestation at offender expense
exceptions: Licensed timber operations under approved forest management plans
Subsistence firewood collection within prescribed limits

quiz.q: Why are saxaul forests particularly important in Kazakhstan?
options: They prevent desertification in the Aral Sea region
quiz.explanation: Saxaul forests in Kazakhstan Aral Sea region play a critical role in preventing desertification and stabilizing degraded land.

laws.title: Organized Crime Participation
laws.subtitle: Being a member of a criminal organization
laws.fullDescription: Kazakhstan criminal law prohibits participation in organized criminal groups and criminal organizations. Even membership without direct participation in specific crimes can lead to prosecution. Leadership of organized crime carries significantly enhanced penalties.
laws.penalty: 5 to 15 years imprisonment; up to 20 years for leaders
exceptions: None — knowing membership in criminal organizations is criminal
laws.sourceLabel: Kazakhstan Criminal Code — Organized Crime Chapter

quiz.q: In Kazakhstan, can someone be prosecuted for organized crime just for membership?
options: No — must have committed a specific crime
Yes — knowing membership is criminal even without direct crime
quiz.explanation: Kazakhstan law makes knowing membership in criminal organizations criminal, even without direct participation in specific offenses.

laws.title: Unlicensed Banking Operations
laws.subtitle: Providing financial services without a National Bank license
laws.fullDescription: Kazakhstan banking law requires all deposit-taking institutions and lending organizations above specified thresholds to obtain licenses from the National Bank of Kazakhstan. Operating financial services without proper licensing undermines financial stability and consumer protection.
laws.penalty: Fine of up to 2,000 MCI; up to 5 years imprisonment for organizers
exceptions: Credit cooperatives below threshold operating under specific framework
Microfinancing organizations under separate regulatory framework
laws.sourceLabel: Kazakhstan Law on Banks and Banking Activity

quiz.q: Which body licenses banking operations in Kazakhstan?
quiz.explanation: The National Bank of Kazakhstan is responsible for licensing and supervising banking operations in the country.

laws.title: Littering in Public Spaces
laws.subtitle: Disposing of waste outside designated areas
laws.fullDescription: Kazakhstan administrative law prohibits littering in public spaces, parks, and streets. Local authorities enforce these rules and communities have been increasingly vocal about environmental cleanliness. Repeat offenders face escalating fines.
laws.penalty: Fine of 3 to 10 MCI
exceptions: Accidental spills with immediate cleanup
Compostable organic material in natural settings

quiz.q: What does Kazakhstan do to repeat litterers?
quiz.explanation: Kazakhstan applies escalating fines to repeat littering offenders to deter the behavior effectively.

laws.title: Illegal Online Gambling
laws.subtitle: Operating or participating in unlicensed online gambling
laws.fullDescription: Kazakhstan gambling law restricts online gambling platforms. Only platforms operating from approved special economic zones in Kapchagay and Shchuchinsk-Borovoye resort areas may offer certain gambling services. Online gambling platforms not meeting these criteria are illegal.
laws.penalty: Fine of 100 to 500 MCI; criminal charges for organizers
exceptions: Gambling platforms physically located in Kazakhstan licensed gambling zones

quiz.q: Where are legal gambling operations concentrated in Kazakhstan?
options: Special economic zones in resort areas
quiz.explanation: Legal gambling in Kazakhstan is restricted to special economic zones in approved resort areas like Kapchagay.

laws.title: Illegal Surveillance
laws.subtitle: Conducting unauthorized electronic surveillance of individuals
laws.fullDescription: Kazakhstan law prohibits private individuals and unauthorized entities from conducting surveillance through wiretapping, electronic monitoring, or location tracking without judicial authorization. State agencies may conduct surveillance only under strict legal procedures.
laws.penalty: Fine; up to 3 years imprisonment
exceptions: Law enforcement surveillance under valid judicial warrants
Parental monitoring of minor children within reasonable limits

quiz.q: Under what condition may law enforcement conduct electronic surveillance in Kazakhstan?
quiz.explanation: Law enforcement surveillance in Kazakhstan requires a valid judicial warrant, ensuring judicial oversight of surveillance activities.

laws.title: Customs Fraud
laws.subtitle: Falsifying customs declarations to avoid duties
laws.fullDescription: Kazakhstan customs law requires accurate declaration of all goods imported or exported. Deliberately undervaluing goods, misdeclaring quantities or categories, or using fraudulent documents to avoid customs duties constitutes customs fraud.
laws.penalty: Fine equal to the evaded duty amount; up to 5 years imprisonment for large-scale fraud
exceptions: Good-faith declaration errors with voluntary correction

quiz.q: What is the financial basis for calculating fines for customs fraud in Kazakhstan?
quiz.explanation: Fines for customs fraud in Kazakhstan are calculated based on the amount of duty evaded, incentivizing full disclosure.

laws.title: Bioweapons Development
laws.subtitle: Creating or stockpiling biological weapons
laws.fullDescription: Kazakhstan, as a signatory to the Biological Weapons Convention, strictly prohibits the development, production, stockpiling, or transfer of biological weapons and agents. Kazakhstan has a complex history with Soviet-era biological weapons programs, making this prohibition especially significant.
laws.penalty: 10 to 20 years imprisonment; life imprisonment if mass casualties result
exceptions: Legitimate biological research under Biosafety Level controls with international oversight
laws.sourceLabel: Kazakhstan Criminal Code — Weapons of Mass Destruction

quiz.q: What historical factor makes Kazakhstan bioweapons laws particularly significant?
options: Soviet-era biological weapons programs on its territory
Proximity to a bioweapons producing state
quiz.explanation: Soviet-era biological weapons programs were operated on Kazakhstan territory, making its prohibition of such weapons especially meaningful.

laws.title: Insider Trading
laws.subtitle: Trading securities based on material non-public information
laws.fullDescription: Kazakhstan securities law prohibits using material non-public information to trade in securities or advise others to do so. Company insiders, employees, and any persons who obtain confidential information must not exploit it for trading advantage.
laws.penalty: Fine of 500 to 2,000 MCI; up to 5 years imprisonment
exceptions: Pre-scheduled automated trading programs set before acquisition of inside information

quiz.q: Who is prohibited from insider trading in Kazakhstan?
options: Any person who obtains material non-public information
quiz.explanation: Any person — not just company insiders — who obtains material non-public information is prohibited from trading on it in Kazakhstan.

laws.title: Hostage Taking
laws.subtitle: Seizing and holding a person to compel action by others
laws.fullDescription: Kazakhstan criminal law criminalizes taking persons hostage to compel governments, organizations, or individuals to take or refrain from taking certain actions. This is treated as a serious violent crime regardless of whether demands are ultimately met.
laws.penalty: 8 to 15 years imprisonment; up to 20 years if the victim is harmed
exceptions: None — hostage taking in any form is criminal

quiz.q: Does it matter whether hostage demands are met when determining guilt in Kazakhstan?
options: Yes — if demands are met, charges are reduced
No — hostage taking is criminal regardless of outcome
quiz.explanation: Hostage taking is criminal in Kazakhstan regardless of whether the demands made are ultimately met or not.

laws.title: Mercenary Activity
laws.subtitle: Participating in armed conflict for financial gain
laws.fullDescription: Kazakhstan criminal law prohibits serving as a mercenary — participating in armed conflicts in foreign countries for monetary compensation when one has no nationality or residency connection to either party. This aligns with international humanitarian law.
laws.penalty: 5 to 15 years imprisonment
exceptions: Citizens serving in state military forces
UN peacekeeping operations under government authorization

quiz.q: What distinguishes a mercenary from a lawful combatant under Kazakhstan law?
options: Serving for pay with no nationality connection to the conflict
quiz.explanation: A mercenary is defined by serving for pay in a conflict without a nationality or residency connection — which is prohibited by Kazakhstan law.

laws.title: Unauthorized Medical Device Sales
laws.subtitle: Selling medical equipment without required certification
laws.fullDescription: Kazakhstan requires medical devices to be registered with the health authorities and meet safety standards before sale. Selling unregistered or uncertified medical devices exposes patients to serious health risks from faulty or ineffective equipment.
laws.penalty: Fine of 50 to 200 MCI; confiscation of devices
exceptions: Emergency import of critical devices under expedited authorization
laws.sourceLabel: Kazakhstan Code on Public Health — Medical Devices

quiz.q: What must medical devices undergo before they can be sold in Kazakhstan?
quiz.explanation: Medical devices must be registered with Kazakhstan health authorities and meet safety standards before they can be legally sold.

laws.title: Industrial Safety Crimes
laws.subtitle: Gross violations causing industrial accidents with casualties
laws.fullDescription: Kazakhstan criminal law holds individuals criminally responsible for gross violations of industrial safety rules that cause serious accidents, injuries, or deaths. Managers, engineers, and safety officers can be prosecuted when negligence leads to industrial disasters.
laws.penalty: 3 to 10 years imprisonment; ban on holding relevant positions
exceptions: Unforeseeable force majeure events despite all precautions taken

quiz.q: Who can be held criminally responsible for industrial accidents in Kazakhstan?
options: Only those who directly caused the accident
quiz.explanation: Kazakhstan holds managers, engineers, and safety officers criminally responsible when negligence contributes to industrial accidents.

laws.title: Land Degradation and Desertification
laws.subtitle: Causing or accelerating land degradation through unsustainable practices
laws.fullDescription: Kazakhstan faces serious desertification challenges, especially following the Aral Sea crisis. Activities that cause or accelerate land degradation — such as overgrazing, unsustainable farming, or improper waste disposal — are subject to environmental liability.
laws.penalty: Fine of 100 to 1,000 MCI; mandatory remediation
exceptions: Natural environmental processes
Approved scientific land use studies

quiz.q: What historical environmental disaster makes land degradation laws especially important in Kazakhstan?
quiz.explanation: The Aral Sea crisis — one of the worst environmental disasters in history — makes Kazakhstan particularly sensitive to land degradation laws.

laws.title: Sale of Substandard Cosmetics
laws.subtitle: Marketing cosmetics with undisclosed harmful ingredients
laws.fullDescription: Kazakhstan consumer safety law requires cosmetic products to meet safety standards and be tested before market release. Selling cosmetics with undisclosed harmful ingredients, exceeding permitted substance concentrations, or making false safety claims is prohibited.
laws.penalty: Fine of 20 to 100 MCI; product recall
exceptions: Research samples clearly marked as experimental and not for sale
laws.sourceLabel: Kazakhstan Code on Public Health — Product Safety

quiz.q: What must cosmetics undergo before they can be legally marketed in Kazakhstan?
quiz.explanation: Cosmetics must undergo safety testing and meet regulatory standards before they can be legally marketed in Kazakhstan.

laws.title: Document Forgery
laws.subtitle: Creating or using falsified official documents
laws.fullDescription: Kazakhstan criminal law prohibits the forgery of official documents, including identity cards, academic certificates, medical records, and government permits. Both creating forgeries and knowingly using them constitute criminal offenses.
laws.penalty: Up to 4 years imprisonment; up to 6 years for forgery used to commit other crimes
exceptions: Theatrical props and artistic reproductions clearly marked as such

quiz.q: What increases the penalty for document forgery in Kazakhstan?
options: Using the forgery to commit other crimes
quiz.explanation: Using forged documents to facilitate other crimes increases the penalty for forgery from up to 4 to up to 6 years.

laws.title: Credit Card Fraud
laws.subtitle: Using stolen or counterfeit payment cards
laws.fullDescription: Kazakhstan criminal law prohibits the manufacture, possession, or use of counterfeit payment cards, as well as using stolen card details for unauthorized transactions. Electronic payment fraud causes significant harm to consumers and financial institutions.
laws.penalty: Fine; 2 to 6 years imprisonment depending on scale
exceptions: Authorized testing of payment systems by card issuers

quiz.q: What activities constitute credit card fraud under Kazakhstan law?
options: Using stolen card details for purchases
Using a credit card for cash advance
quiz.explanation: Using stolen payment card details for unauthorized transactions is credit card fraud under Kazakhstan criminal law.

laws.title: Sabotage of Critical Infrastructure
laws.subtitle: Damaging or disrupting essential state infrastructure
laws.fullDescription: Kazakhstan criminal law treats the sabotage of critical infrastructure — including power grids, pipelines, communications networks, water systems, and transportation — as a serious crime against the state. Given Kazakhstan energy export dependencies, pipeline security is particularly emphasized.
laws.penalty: 8 to 20 years imprisonment; up to life imprisonment if mass casualties
exceptions: None — intentional sabotage is always criminal
laws.sourceLabel: Kazakhstan Criminal Code — State Security Crimes

quiz.q: Why are pipeline security laws especially important in Kazakhstan?
options: Kazakhstan energy exports depend heavily on pipeline infrastructure
Pipelines are owned by foreign companies
quiz.explanation: Kazakhstan major oil and gas export revenues depend on pipeline infrastructure, making pipeline security a national economic priority.

laws.title: Cattle Rustling
laws.subtitle: Stealing livestock from farms and ranches
laws.fullDescription: Livestock theft has been a significant concern in Kazakhstan vast steppe regions where herding is a traditional way of life. Stealing cattle, horses, sheep, or other livestock causes serious economic harm to rural families and communities.
laws.penalty: Fine; 3 to 7 years imprisonment depending on scale
exceptions: Good-faith recovery of own livestock from neighboring lands

quiz.q: Why is livestock theft particularly serious in Kazakhstan rural context?
options: Kazakhstan exports most of its meat
Herding is a traditional livelihood and livestock loss is devastating for families
Horses are sacred in Kazakh culture
Kazakhstan has few livestock insurance options
quiz.explanation: In Kazakhstan steppe regions, livestock represents the primary livelihood for herding families, making theft economically devastating.

laws.title: Aircraft Hijacking
laws.subtitle: Unlawfully seizing control of an aircraft
laws.fullDescription: Kazakhstan criminal law, consistent with international aviation conventions, criminalizes the unlawful seizure or exercise of control over an aircraft in flight. This applies regardless of whether violence is used and regardless of the aircraft registration.
laws.penalty: 10 to 20 years imprisonment; up to life imprisonment if fatalities occur
exceptions: None — aircraft hijacking is always criminal

quiz.q: Does Kazakhstan anti-hijacking law apply to foreign aircraft?
quiz.explanation: Kazakhstan anti-hijacking law, consistent with international conventions, applies regardless of the aircraft national registration.

laws.title: Fraudulent Real Estate Advertising
laws.subtitle: Misrepresenting properties in sales listings
laws.fullDescription: Kazakhstan consumer protection law prohibits false or misleading advertising in real estate sales and rentals. This includes exaggerating property features, hiding material defects, misrepresenting location, and using manipulated photos in listings.
laws.penalty: Fine of 50 to 200 MCI; civil liability for damages
exceptions: Honest opinion statements about a property clearly labeled as such

quiz.q: What real estate advertising practice is specifically prohibited in Kazakhstan?
quiz.explanation: Deliberately hiding material defects of a property in real estate advertising is prohibited under Kazakhstan consumer protection law.

laws.title: Illegal Wildlife Trade
laws.subtitle: Buying, selling, or capturing protected species
laws.fullDescription: Kazakhstan is home to numerous protected species including snow leopards, saigas, steppe eagles, and Siberian cranes. Trading in protected animals or their parts — fur, feathers, bones — is prohibited under national law and international conventions.
laws.penalty: Fine of 100 to 500 MCI; up to 3 years imprisonment
exceptions: Licensed scientific research with proper permits
Approved captive breeding programs

quiz.q: Which iconic species is particularly protected under Kazakhstan wildlife laws?
quiz.explanation: The snow leopard is among Kazakhstan most protected species, with strict penalties for any trade in these endangered animals.

laws.title: Discrimination in Employment
laws.subtitle: Refusing to hire or unfairly dismissing workers based on protected characteristics
laws.fullDescription: Kazakhstan labor law prohibits employment discrimination based on nationality, gender, age, religion, disability, or other protected characteristics. Employers must base hiring and employment decisions on professional qualifications and job requirements.
laws.penalty: Fine of 20 to 100 MCI; reinstatement and compensation for dismissed workers
exceptions: Genuine occupational requirements, such as requiring physical fitness for physically demanding roles

quiz.q: On what basis must Kazakhstan employers make employment decisions?
quiz.explanation: Kazakhstan law requires employers to base employment decisions on professional qualifications and job requirements, not personal characteristics.

laws.title: Embezzlement of State Funds
laws.subtitle: Misappropriating public funds by officials
laws.fullDescription: Kazakhstan criminal law harshly punishes the misappropriation of state funds by public officials. Given concerns about corruption in public institutions, embezzlement of budget funds, state enterprise assets, or public property carries severe penalties.
laws.penalty: 5 to 12 years imprisonment; full restitution; permanent ban from public office
exceptions: None — misappropriation of public funds is always criminal
laws.sourceLabel: Kazakhstan Criminal Code — Corruption and Embezzlement

quiz.q: What additional consequence accompanies imprisonment for embezzlement of state funds?
quiz.explanation: Beyond imprisonment, embezzlement of state funds results in a permanent ban from holding public office in Kazakhstan.

laws.title: Illegal Sale of Prescription Drugs
laws.subtitle: Dispensing prescription medicines without valid prescriptions
laws.fullDescription: Kazakhstan pharmacy law requires that prescription medicines be dispensed only with valid medical prescriptions from licensed healthcare providers. Selling prescription drugs without prescriptions endangers public health by enabling misuse and self-medication.
laws.penalty: Fine of 50 to 300 MCI; pharmacy license revocation
exceptions: Emergency dispensing of life-saving medications in situations where delay would cause death
laws.sourceLabel: Kazakhstan Code on Public Health — Pharmaceuticals

quiz.q: When can pharmacies in Kazakhstan dispense prescription drugs without a prescription?
quiz.explanation: Kazakhstan pharmacy law permits prescription-free dispensing only in genuine emergency situations where delay would cause death.

laws.title: Fraud in Commercial Transactions
laws.subtitle: Deceiving parties in business dealings for financial gain
laws.fullDescription: Kazakhstan criminal law prohibits deliberate deception in commercial transactions, including misrepresenting the quality or quantity of goods, false invoicing, and fraudulent contract performance. Commercial fraud damages business trust and economic activity.
laws.penalty: Fine; 2 to 7 years imprisonment depending on scale
exceptions: Good-faith mistakes and genuine disputes about contract performance

quiz.q: What distinguishes criminal commercial fraud from a civil contract dispute in Kazakhstan?
quiz.explanation: Criminal fraud requires deliberate deception, distinguishing it from good-faith contract disputes handled through civil law.

laws.title: Crimes Against Humanity
laws.subtitle: Systematic attacks on civilian populations
laws.fullDescription: Kazakhstan criminal law incorporates international crimes against humanity, including murder, torture, deportation, imprisonment, and persecution of civilian populations as part of a systematic attack. Kazakhstan cooperates with the International Criminal Court on such matters.
laws.penalty: 15 to 20 years imprisonment; life imprisonment for most severe cases
exceptions: None — crimes against humanity are never justified

quiz.q: What makes an act a crime against humanity rather than an ordinary crime?
options: Being part of a systematic attack on civilian populations
quiz.explanation: Crimes against humanity are defined by being part of a widespread or systematic attack directed against a civilian population.

laws.title: Illegal Currency Exchange Operations
laws.subtitle: Operating unauthorized foreign exchange services
laws.fullDescription: Kazakhstan currency control law requires all foreign exchange transactions above minimal amounts to be conducted through licensed banks and exchange offices. Operating unauthorized currency exchange points or exchanging currency at unofficial rates is prohibited.
laws.penalty: Fine of 100 to 300 MCI; confiscation of currency
exceptions: Small private foreign currency transactions below threshold amounts

quiz.q: Where must Kazakhstanis conduct foreign exchange transactions?
quiz.explanation: Kazakhstan currency regulations require foreign exchange transactions to be conducted through licensed banks and exchange offices.

laws.title: Piracy and Armed Robbery at Sea
laws.subtitle: Attacking or robbing vessels at sea
laws.fullDescription: Kazakhstan Caspian Sea jurisdiction includes the criminalization of piracy and armed robbery against vessels. While rare historically, Kazakhstan cooperates with other Caspian states to maintain maritime security under the Caspian Sea legal regime.
laws.penalty: 10 to 20 years imprisonment
exceptions: None — piracy is always criminal under domestic and international law

quiz.q: Which body of water does Kazakhstan piracy law primarily address?
quiz.explanation: Kazakhstan piracy laws primarily address the Caspian Sea, where it has jurisdiction and cooperates with other Caspian states.

laws.title: Academic Plagiarism for Degrees
laws.subtitle: Submitting copied work to obtain academic credentials
laws.fullDescription: Kazakhstan higher education law prohibits the submission of plagiarized work for academic degrees. Using ghost-writing services, submitting another person work as one own, or copying without attribution to obtain academic credentials is academic fraud subject to penalties.
laws.penalty: Expulsion from institution; diploma revocation if fraud discovered after graduation
exceptions: Properly attributed quotations and references
Collaborative work clearly identified as such

quiz.q: What happens in Kazakhstan if plagiarism is discovered after a degree is awarded?
quiz.explanation: In Kazakhstan, diplomas obtained through plagiarism or academic fraud can be revoked even after they have been awarded.

laws.title: Chemical Weapons Possession
laws.subtitle: Possessing or developing chemical warfare agents
laws.fullDescription: Kazakhstan, as a signatory to the Chemical Weapons Convention, strictly prohibits development, production, stockpiling, and use of chemical weapons. Kazakhstan has historical connections to Soviet chemical weapons programs, making enforcement particularly sensitive.
laws.penalty: 10 to 20 years imprisonment; life imprisonment if used
exceptions: Industrial chemicals for legitimate purposes with proper safety measures

quiz.q: What international agreement underlies Kazakhstan ban on chemical weapons?
quiz.explanation: Kazakhstan ban on chemical weapons reflects its obligations under the Chemical Weapons Convention, which it has signed and ratified.

laws.title: Theft of Cultural Property
laws.subtitle: Stealing or illegally exporting national heritage items
laws.fullDescription: Kazakhstan law protects its rich cultural heritage including archaeological finds, historical artifacts, and traditional art. Stealing cultural property from museums, historical sites, or private collections, or illegally exporting such items, is a serious criminal offense.
laws.penalty: 3 to 10 years imprisonment; mandatory return of items
exceptions: Official loans and cultural exchanges under bilateral agreements

quiz.q: What must happen to stolen cultural property recovered in Kazakhstan?
options: It is auctioned to fund museums
It is kept by the finder
It must be returned to its rightful owner or state
It is destroyed if of uncertain origin
quiz.explanation: Stolen cultural property in Kazakhstan must be returned to its rightful owner or to the state, along with criminal penalties for the thief.

laws.title: Water Supply Contamination
laws.subtitle: Polluting drinking water sources
laws.fullDescription: Kazakhstan criminal law prohibits the contamination of water supply sources — including rivers, lakes, reservoirs, and groundwater used for drinking water. Given water scarcity in many Kazakhstani regions, protecting drinking water sources is a priority.
laws.penalty: Fine; up to 5 years imprisonment if public health affected
exceptions: Accidental contamination with immediate reporting and remediation

quiz.q: Why is drinking water protection particularly important in Kazakhstan?
options: Kazakhstan has the most rivers in Central Asia
Water scarcity affects many regions of the country
Kazakhstan sells water to neighboring countries
Ground water is owned by the state exclusively
quiz.explanation: Water scarcity affects many Kazakhstani regions, making the protection of drinking water sources a national priority.

laws.title: Burglary
laws.subtitle: Breaking into buildings to commit theft
laws.fullDescription: Kazakhstan criminal law distinguishes between theft and burglary — the latter involving unlawful entry into homes, businesses, or other premises. Breaking and entering with intent to steal carries enhanced penalties compared to simple theft.
laws.penalty: 3 to 7 years imprisonment; up to 10 years for aggravated burglary
exceptions: None for intentional breaking and entering with criminal intent

quiz.q: What distinguishes burglary from simple theft in Kazakhstan law?
options: The time of day it occurred
quiz.explanation: Burglary in Kazakhstan is distinguished from theft by the unlawful entry into premises, which carries enhanced penalties.

laws.title: Illegal Greenhouse Gas Emissions
laws.subtitle: Exceeding permitted carbon emission limits
laws.fullDescription: Kazakhstan has implemented carbon market mechanisms and emission limits for major industrial installations. Exceeding permitted greenhouse gas emission quotas without purchasing sufficient emission allowances violates environmental law.
laws.penalty: Fine proportional to excess emissions; suspension of operations for repeat violations
exceptions: Force majeure operational situations with immediate reporting

quiz.q: What mechanism does Kazakhstan use to manage industrial greenhouse gas emissions?
options: Carbon market with emission quotas and allowances
quiz.explanation: Kazakhstan has implemented a carbon market system where industrial facilities must hold sufficient emission allowances for their actual emissions.

laws.title: Obstruction of Justice
laws.subtitle: Interfering with legal proceedings or investigations
laws.fullDescription: Kazakhstan criminal law prohibits obstructing law enforcement investigations and judicial proceedings. This includes tampering with evidence, intimidating witnesses, bribing officials, and helping suspects escape. Such acts undermine the rule of law.
laws.penalty: Up to 6 years imprisonment
exceptions: Legitimate legal defense activities within professional ethics rules

quiz.q: Which activity is NOT considered obstruction of justice in Kazakhstan?
quiz.explanation: Hiring a defense lawyer is a legal right and does not constitute obstruction of justice in Kazakhstan or any country.

laws.title: Power Grid Sabotage
laws.subtitle: Damaging electricity generation or distribution infrastructure
laws.fullDescription: Kazakhstan criminal law specifically addresses sabotage of the power grid, including electricity generation facilities, substations, and transmission lines. Power outages cause widespread harm and can be life-threatening in Kazakhstan extreme winter conditions.
laws.penalty: 8 to 20 years imprisonment; enhanced if casualties result
exceptions: None — intentional damage to power infrastructure is always criminal

quiz.q: Why are power grid attacks particularly dangerous in Kazakhstan?
options: Kazakhstan is the biggest electricity exporter
Power outages in extreme winter can be life-threatening
Power is the main export commodity
quiz.explanation: Kazakhstan extreme winter temperatures make power grid protection especially critical, as outages can be life-threatening.

laws.title: Public Intoxication and Disorderly Conduct
laws.subtitle: Being drunk and disruptive in public spaces
laws.fullDescription: Kazakhstan administrative law prohibits public intoxication and disorderly behavior in public spaces. This includes aggressive behavior, disturbing public peace, and appearing in public in a state of severe intoxication that threatens personal safety or public order.
laws.penalty: Fine of 5 to 20 MCI; administrative detention up to 10 days
exceptions: Medical treatment of alcohol-related conditions in public
Supervised public events where alcohol is legally served
laws.sourceLabel: Kazakhstan Administrative Offences Code — Public Order

quiz.q: Beyond fines, what can happen to severely intoxicated and disorderly persons in Kazakhstan?
quiz.explanation: In addition to fines, severely intoxicated and disorderly persons in Kazakhstan can face administrative detention of up to 10 days.

laws.title: Fraudulent Bankruptcy
laws.subtitle: Concealing assets to avoid paying debts in bankruptcy
laws.fullDescription: Kazakhstan criminal law prohibits fraudulent bankruptcy — the deliberate concealment of assets, falsification of accounting records, or other schemes to avoid paying legitimate creditors during insolvency proceedings. This harms creditors and undermines financial markets.
laws.penalty: 3 to 7 years imprisonment; full restitution of concealed assets
exceptions: Good-faith insolvency without intent to defraud

quiz.q: What is the key element that makes bankruptcy fraudulent under Kazakhstan law?
options: Deliberately concealing assets to avoid paying creditors
quiz.explanation: Fraudulent bankruptcy requires deliberate concealment of assets — distinguishing it from honest insolvency which is not criminal.

laws.title: Cyberstalking and Online Harassment
laws.subtitle: Using technology to stalk or harass individuals
laws.fullDescription: Kazakhstan criminal law addresses the use of information and communication technologies to stalk, harass, or threaten individuals. This includes persistent unwanted contact, distributing private images, and making threats through electronic means.
laws.penalty: Fine; up to 2 years imprisonment; up to 5 years if threats are serious
exceptions: Legitimate journalism and public interest investigations using public information

quiz.q: What type of online behavior constitutes cyberstalking in Kazakhstan?
options: Persistent unwanted contact through digital means
quiz.explanation: Cyberstalking involves persistent unwanted contact through digital means — distinguishing it from occasional criticism or public information sharing.

laws.title: Medical Negligence Causing Death
laws.subtitle: Gross medical negligence resulting in patient death
laws.fullDescription: Kazakhstan criminal law holds medical professionals criminally responsible when gross negligence — departing significantly from accepted medical standards — causes patient death or serious harm. This promotes accountability while recognizing the complexity of medical decision-making.
laws.penalty: Up to 5 years imprisonment; medical license revocation
exceptions: Honest errors within the bounds of accepted medical practice
Unforeseeable complications despite appropriate care

quiz.q: What standard distinguishes criminal medical negligence from a civil malpractice claim in Kazakhstan?
options: Gross departure from accepted medical standards
Whether the patient signed consent forms
quiz.explanation: Criminal medical negligence in Kazakhstan requires gross departure from accepted standards — mere mistakes resulting in harm are handled civilly.

laws.title: Illegal Mining Operations
laws.subtitle: Extracting minerals without proper licenses
laws.fullDescription: Kazakhstan is rich in mineral resources, and mining is strictly regulated to protect the environment and ensure state revenue. Operating mining without proper licenses, environmental permits, and safety compliance is a serious criminal offense.
laws.penalty: Fine; 3 to 8 years imprisonment for large-scale illegal mining
exceptions: Small-scale artisan mining under specific frameworks in designated areas

quiz.q: What type of mining is sometimes permitted under exceptions in Kazakhstan?
options: Small-scale artisan mining in designated areas
quiz.explanation: Small-scale artisan mining may be permitted in designated areas under specific regulatory frameworks in Kazakhstan.

laws.title: Unauthorized Photography of Individuals
laws.subtitle: Taking and publishing photos of people without consent
laws.fullDescription: Kazakhstan civil and criminal law protects individuals right to their image. Photographing individuals in private settings without consent, and publishing such images without permission, violates privacy rights. Sharing intimate images without consent carries enhanced criminal penalties.
laws.penalty: Fine; up to 3 years imprisonment for non-consensual intimate image sharing
exceptions: Photography in public places where consent is implied
Journalism covering public interest events

quiz.q: What type of unauthorized image sharing carries the most serious penalties in Kazakhstan?
quiz.explanation: Non-consensual sharing of intimate images carries enhanced criminal penalties in Kazakhstan, reflecting the serious harm it causes victims.

laws.title: Counterfeit Goods Production
laws.subtitle: Manufacturing fake branded products
laws.fullDescription: Kazakhstan intellectual property law and consumer protection law both prohibit the production and sale of counterfeit goods bearing trademarked brands without authorization. The production of counterfeit consumer goods, including luxury items, electronics, and medicines, is criminalized.
laws.penalty: Fine of 100 to 500 MCI; seizure and destruction of goods; up to 3 years imprisonment
exceptions: Licensed manufacturers producing genuine goods under agreement
laws.sourceLabel: Kazakhstan Law on Copyright and Trademarks

quiz.q: Beyond financial penalties, what happens to counterfeit goods seized in Kazakhstan?
quiz.explanation: Counterfeit goods seized in Kazakhstan are subject to destruction, not redistribution, to prevent them from re-entering commerce.

laws.title: Kidnapping for Ransom
laws.subtitle: Abducting a person to extort money from their family
laws.fullDescription: Kazakhstan criminal law treats kidnapping for ransom as a particularly serious crime. Abducting individuals and holding them to extort money from families or organizations causes severe psychological trauma and physical danger.
laws.penalty: 8 to 15 years imprisonment; up to 20 years if victim harmed
exceptions: None — kidnapping is always criminal

quiz.q: What increases the penalty for kidnapping beyond the base sentence in Kazakhstan?
options: Using a vehicle in the crime
quiz.explanation: Physical harm to the kidnapping victim increases the maximum penalty to 20 years in Kazakhstan.

laws.title: Payroll Tax Fraud
laws.subtitle: Failing to pay employment taxes on wages
laws.fullDescription: Kazakhstan employers are required to withhold and remit social contributions and individual income tax from employee wages. Failing to do so — or reporting false payroll figures — deprives the social insurance system of needed funds.
laws.penalty: Fine of 100 to 300 MCI; up to 4 years imprisonment for large-scale fraud
exceptions: Good-faith calculation errors with prompt correction when identified

quiz.q: What obligation do Kazakhstan employers have regarding employee taxes?
options: Employees pay their own taxes directly
Employers withhold and remit taxes on employee behalf
Only businesses over 50 employees must withhold
quiz.explanation: Kazakhstan employers must withhold income tax and social contributions from wages and remit them to the relevant authorities on employees behalf.

laws.title: Cyber Attacks on Government Systems
laws.subtitle: Hacking or disrupting official government digital infrastructure
laws.fullDescription: Kazakhstan criminal law imposes especially severe penalties for cyber attacks targeting government information systems, electoral systems, and national security infrastructure. Such attacks threaten state sovereignty and public services.
laws.penalty: Up to 10 years imprisonment; up to 15 years if significant disruption caused
exceptions: Authorized government security testing by certified agencies

quiz.q: What factor most significantly increases penalties for hacking in Kazakhstan?
quiz.explanation: Targeting government information systems carries the highest cybercrime penalties in Kazakhstan, reflecting the threat to state functions.

laws.title: Illegal Slaughter of Animals
laws.subtitle: Slaughtering livestock outside licensed facilities
laws.fullDescription: Kazakhstan food safety and veterinary law requires that livestock intended for human consumption be slaughtered in licensed facilities that meet hygiene, animal welfare, and food safety standards. Unauthorized slaughter creates food safety risks.
laws.penalty: Fine of 20 to 100 MCI; closure of unauthorized facility
exceptions: Home slaughter for personal family consumption within traditional practices

quiz.q: What is the key requirement for lawful commercial livestock slaughter in Kazakhstan?
quiz.explanation: Commercial livestock slaughter in Kazakhstan must occur in licensed facilities that meet hygiene, welfare, and food safety standards.

laws.title: Incitement to Interethnic Hatred
laws.subtitle: Promoting hostility between different ethnic groups
laws.fullDescription: Kazakhstan, with its diverse multi-ethnic population including Kazakhs, Russians, Uzbeks, and many other groups, has laws prohibiting deliberate incitement to hatred, discrimination, or violence on the basis of ethnicity, nationality, or race.
laws.penalty: Fine; up to 5 years imprisonment; up to 7 years if violence results
exceptions: Academic study of ethnic tensions
Journalism reporting on interethnic issues factually

quiz.q: Why does Kazakhstan have specific laws against ethnic incitement?
options: It has only two ethnic groups
Its multi-ethnic population makes interethnic harmony a national priority
It is required by EU membership
Ethnic conflict is its most common crime
quiz.explanation: Kazakhstan multi-ethnic population — including many nationalities — makes laws protecting interethnic harmony a national priority.

laws.title: Murder
laws.subtitle: Unlawful killing of another person
laws.fullDescription: Murder is one of the most serious crimes under Kazakhstan criminal law. The deliberate, unlawful taking of human life carries the most severe penalties available under Kazakhstan justice system. Aggravating circumstances such as premeditation, multiple victims, or cruelty increase the sentence.
laws.penalty: 10 to 20 years imprisonment; life imprisonment for aggravated murder
exceptions: Justified self-defense within proportionate limits
Accidental death without negligence
laws.sourceLabel: Kazakhstan Criminal Code — Crimes Against Life

quiz.q: What is the maximum penalty for aggravated murder in Kazakhstan?
quiz.explanation: Aggravated murder in Kazakhstan carries life imprisonment. Kazakhstan abolished the death penalty in 2021.

laws.title: Arson
laws.subtitle: Deliberately setting fire to property
laws.fullDescription: Kazakhstan criminal law criminalizes the deliberate setting of fires to destroy property. Arson endangers human lives, destroys property, and can have catastrophic consequences. The severity of penalties depends on whether people were endangered or killed.
laws.penalty: 3 to 8 years imprisonment; up to 15 years if people are harmed or killed
exceptions: Controlled burns with proper permits on own agricultural land
laws.sourceLabel: Kazakhstan Criminal Code — Destruction of Property

quiz.q: What factor most increases the arson penalty in Kazakhstan?
quiz.explanation: Arson resulting in human casualties carries the highest penalty of up to 15 years imprisonment in Kazakhstan.

laws.title: Recruitment of Children for Criminal Purposes
laws.subtitle: Involving minors in criminal activities
laws.fullDescription: Kazakhstan criminal law prohibits recruiting, inducing, or involving children in criminal activities. Adults who use minors as tools for crime — whether in drug trafficking, theft, or any other offense — face enhanced penalties for corrupting young people.
laws.penalty: 5 to 10 years imprisonment
exceptions: None — any involvement of children in criminal schemes is an aggravating factor
laws.sourceLabel: Kazakhstan Criminal Code — Crimes Against Minors

quiz.q: How does involving children affect criminal penalties in Kazakhstan?
options: It reduces penalties due to coercion
It has no effect on penalties
It is an aggravating factor increasing penalties
It transfers liability to the child
quiz.explanation: Using children in criminal schemes is an aggravating factor in Kazakhstan, leading to significantly enhanced penalties for adult offenders.

laws.title: Oil Spill Negligence
laws.subtitle: Failing to prevent or contain petroleum spills
laws.fullDescription: Kazakhstan oil and gas industry is strictly regulated to prevent environmental catastrophes. Companies that negligently allow oil spills — whether through improper equipment maintenance, inadequate safety procedures, or failure to contain leaks — face serious civil and criminal liability.
laws.penalty: Fine of up to 10,000 MCI; criminal charges for gross negligence; mandatory remediation
exceptions: Natural disasters causing spills despite all reasonable precautions

quiz.q: What is the primary environmental concern associated with Kazakhstan oil industry?
options: Soil and water contamination from spills
quiz.explanation: Oil spills in Kazakhstan can contaminate vast areas of soil and water, posing serious environmental risks in the steppe ecosystem.

laws.title: Breaking and Entering
laws.subtitle: Unlawfully entering a premises without permission
laws.fullDescription: Kazakhstan criminal law prohibits unlawful entry into homes, businesses, or other premises without the owner consent. Even without intent to steal, unauthorized entry violates property rights and personal security.
laws.penalty: Fine; up to 2 years imprisonment; up to 5 years if entering a home
exceptions: Emergency entry to prevent greater harm, such as rescuing someone in danger
Law enforcement entry with proper judicial authorization

quiz.q: Which type of unlawful entry carries the highest penalty in Kazakhstan?
quiz.explanation: Unlawfully entering a private home carries the most serious penalty for breaking and entering under Kazakhstan law.

laws.title: Illegal Intelligence Collection
laws.subtitle: Conducting espionage activities for a foreign power
laws.fullDescription: Kazakhstan criminalizes the gathering of intelligence information for foreign governments or organizations without authorization. This includes electronic surveillance, recruiting informants, and collecting sensitive information with intent to benefit a foreign power.
laws.penalty: 10 to 15 years imprisonment
exceptions: Authorized intelligence exchange under bilateral agreements

quiz.q: What is the key element of illegal intelligence collection in Kazakhstan?
options: Gathering information to benefit a foreign power
quiz.explanation: Illegal intelligence collection in Kazakhstan is defined by intent to benefit a foreign power — distinguishing it from lawful research.

laws.title: Unauthorized Clinical Trials
laws.subtitle: Conducting medical research on humans without proper ethics approval
laws.fullDescription: Kazakhstan medical research law requires that clinical trials involving human subjects receive prior approval from an ethics committee and be conducted under strict protocols protecting participant rights, safety, and informed consent.
laws.penalty: Fine; up to 4 years imprisonment if harm results
exceptions: Emergency compassionate use under expedited review procedures
laws.sourceLabel: Kazakhstan Code on Public Health — Research Ethics

quiz.q: What body must approve clinical trials before they begin in Kazakhstan?
quiz.explanation: Clinical trials in Kazakhstan require prior approval from an ethics committee to ensure participant rights, safety, and informed consent.

laws.title: Forced Labor
laws.subtitle: Compelling a person to work through coercion or threats
laws.fullDescription: Kazakhstan criminal law prohibits forced labor — compelling a person to perform work or services through violence, threats, deprivation of freedom, or other coercive means. This includes debt bondage and other exploitative labor practices.
laws.penalty: 4 to 10 years imprisonment
exceptions: Community service ordered by court as punishment
Compulsory military service within legal framework

quiz.q: What distinguishes forced labor from voluntary employment in Kazakhstan law?
options: Working more than 40 hours a week
Work performed under coercion or threats
quiz.explanation: Forced labor is defined by coercion or threats — the denial of free choice to refuse or terminate employment is its defining characteristic.

laws.title: Bank Robbery
laws.subtitle: Stealing from financial institutions using threats or force
laws.fullDescription: Kazakhstan criminal law treats robbery of banks and other financial institutions as a particularly serious crime due to the danger to staff and customers, the scale of potential theft, and the destabilizing effect on financial sector trust.
laws.penalty: 8 to 15 years imprisonment; up to 20 years for armed bank robbery
exceptions: None — bank robbery is always a serious violent crime

quiz.q: What increases the penalty for bank robbery in Kazakhstan?
quiz.explanation: Armed bank robbery — using weapons — carries the maximum penalty of up to 20 years imprisonment in Kazakhstan.

laws.title: Emergency Medical Service Obstruction
laws.subtitle: Hindering ambulances or emergency medical personnel
laws.fullDescription: Kazakhstan law protects the ability of emergency medical services to operate effectively. Blocking ambulances, interfering with paramedics, or attacking emergency medical personnel constitutes a serious offense that can cost lives.
laws.penalty: Fine; up to 5 years imprisonment if people are harmed due to obstruction
exceptions: None — interfering with emergency services is always an aggravating factor

quiz.q: Why is obstruction of emergency medical services treated particularly seriously in Kazakhstan?
quiz.explanation: Obstructing emergency medical services is treated seriously because delays in reaching patients can directly result in preventable deaths.

laws.title: Illegal Lotteries and Sweepstakes
laws.subtitle: Running unauthorized prize draws targeting the public
laws.fullDescription: Kazakhstan gambling regulation requires that all lottery and prize-draw operations involving the public be licensed. Operating unauthorized lotteries — including online sweepstakes targeting Kazakh residents — is an administrative and potentially criminal offense.
laws.penalty: Fine of 50 to 200 MCI; seizure of proceeds
exceptions: Small-scale charitable raffles within permitted thresholds

quiz.q: Can charitable organizations run raffles in Kazakhstan without full gambling licenses?
options: No — all lotteries require full licenses
Yes — small-scale charitable raffles within thresholds are permitted
Only if approved by the government annually
quiz.explanation: Small-scale charitable raffles within permitted thresholds can operate without full gambling licenses in Kazakhstan.

laws.title: Treason
laws.subtitle: Betraying the Kazakhstani state to a foreign power
laws.fullDescription: Kazakhstan criminal law defines treason as actions against Kazakhstan sovereignty, constitutional order, or security committed by citizens in favor of a foreign state. This includes espionage, armed rebellion, and sabotage carried out at foreign direction.
laws.penalty: 15 to 20 years imprisonment; life imprisonment in extreme cases
exceptions: None — treason against the state is one of the most serious offenses

quiz.q: Who can be charged with treason under Kazakhstan law?
quiz.explanation: Treason under Kazakhstan law applies to citizens who betray the state — foreigners who commit similar acts face espionage charges instead.

laws.title: Genocide
laws.subtitle: Acts intended to destroy a national, ethnic, or religious group
laws.fullDescription: Kazakhstan criminal law, consistent with the UN Genocide Convention, criminalizes acts committed with intent to destroy in whole or in part a national, ethnic, racial, or religious group. This includes killing group members, causing serious harm, and imposing conditions of destruction.
laws.penalty: Life imprisonment
exceptions: None — genocide admits no legal justification

quiz.q: What is the maximum penalty for genocide under Kazakhstan law?
options: Death penalty — restored for this crime
quiz.explanation: Genocide carries life imprisonment in Kazakhstan. The death penalty was abolished in 2021 and is not applied even for genocide.

laws.title: Electoral Fraud
laws.subtitle: Manipulating elections or vote counts
laws.fullDescription: Kazakhstan electoral law prohibits all forms of electoral fraud including ballot stuffing, vote buying, falsifying election results, or preventing legitimate voters from voting. While international observers have raised concerns about electoral practices, laws formally prohibiting fraud exist.
laws.penalty: Up to 5 years imprisonment; permanent disenfranchisement for officials
exceptions: None — electoral fraud undermines democracy and is always criminal

quiz.q: What additional consequence can electoral officials convicted of fraud face?
quiz.explanation: Electoral officials convicted of fraud in Kazakhstan can face permanent disenfranchisement — being banned from holding office.

laws.title: Violent Home Invasion
laws.subtitle: Forcible entry into a home with violence or threats
laws.fullDescription: Kazakhstan criminal law imposes severe penalties on violent home invasions — forcibly entering a dwelling with violence or threats of violence. This crime violates the sanctity of the home and places residents in extreme fear and danger.
laws.penalty: 5 to 12 years imprisonment
exceptions: None — violent home invasion is always seriously criminal
laws.sourceLabel: Kazakhstan Criminal Code — Violent Property Crimes

quiz.q: What distinguishes violent home invasion from ordinary trespassing under Kazakhstan law?
options: The value of property in the home
The use of violence or threats when entering
quiz.explanation: Violent home invasion is distinguished by the use of force or threats during entry, which significantly increases the seriousness of the offense.

laws.title: Coup Attempt and Unconstitutional Power Seizure
laws.subtitle: Attempting to seize state power by unconstitutional means
laws.fullDescription: Kazakhstan criminal law, reinforced after the January 2022 unrest, prohibits any attempt to seize state power through unconstitutional means. This includes organizing or leading armed groups, coordinating with foreign powers, or inciting mass actions aimed at overthrowing the constitutional order.
laws.penalty: 15 to 20 years imprisonment; life imprisonment for leaders
exceptions: None — unconstitutional seizure of power is the highest state crime
laws.sourceLabel: Kazakhstan Criminal Code — Constitutional Order Crimes

quiz.q: What event in Kazakhstan recent history reinforced laws on unconstitutional power seizure?
quiz.explanation: The January 2022 unrest in Kazakhstan, which saw violent clashes and government claims of coup attempts, reinforced existing laws on unconstitutional power seizure.

laws.title: Vandalism of Historical Monuments
laws.subtitle: Damaging or defacing protected historical sites
laws.fullDescription: Kazakhstan protects its historical monuments, war memorials, and cultural heritage sites by law. Damaging, defacing, or destroying these protected sites — including graffiti on historical structures — is a criminal offense.
laws.penalty: Fine of 20 to 100 MCI; up to 2 years imprisonment for significant damage
exceptions: Authorized restoration and conservation work by licensed professionals
laws.sourceLabel: Kazakhstan Law on Culture — Heritage Protection

quiz.q: Is graffiti on historical monuments a criminal offense in Kazakhstan?
options: Only if the monument is listed nationally
Yes — defacement of protected sites is criminal
Only if graffiti is offensive content
quiz.explanation: Graffiti and other defacement of protected historical monuments constitutes a criminal offense under Kazakhstan cultural heritage law.

laws.title: Import of Invasive Species
laws.subtitle: Bringing non-native species that threaten local ecosystems
laws.fullDescription: Kazakhstan environmental law prohibits the deliberate import of plants, animals, or microorganisms classified as invasive species without strict scientific authorization. Invasive species can devastate native ecosystems and agricultural systems.
laws.penalty: Fine of 30 to 150 MCI; confiscation and destruction of imported organisms
exceptions: Scientific import with strict containment measures and ethics approval

quiz.q: What happens to invasive species that are illegally imported into Kazakhstan?
options: They are returned to the country of origin
quiz.explanation: Illegally imported invasive species in Kazakhstan are confiscated and destroyed to prevent ecosystem damage.

laws.title: Child Abandonment
laws.subtitle: Deserting a child without adequate care
laws.fullDescription: Kazakhstan criminal and family law impose legal duties of care on parents and guardians. Abandoning a child — leaving them without adequate supervision, food, shelter, or care — constitutes both a child protection violation and a criminal offense.
laws.penalty: Up to 2 years imprisonment; loss of parental rights
exceptions: Safe surrender to hospitals or child services without criminal intent to harm

quiz.q: What civil consequence accompanies criminal punishment for child abandonment in Kazakhstan?
options: Financial penalty to child support fund
quiz.explanation: In addition to criminal penalties, parents convicted of child abandonment in Kazakhstan may permanently lose their parental rights.

laws.title: Illegal Migration Organization
laws.subtitle: Organizing illegal border crossing for profit
laws.fullDescription: Kazakhstan criminal law prohibits organized smuggling of migrants across borders. This includes arranging transportation, providing falsified documents, and operating safe houses for illegal migrants for financial gain. Organized smuggling networks exploit vulnerable people.
laws.penalty: 5 to 12 years imprisonment; up to 15 years for organized networks
exceptions: Humanitarian assistance to refugees not motivated by financial gain

quiz.q: What distinguishes criminal migration organization from humanitarian refugee assistance in Kazakhstan?
quiz.explanation: Kazakhstan law distinguishes profit-motivated smuggling from genuine humanitarian assistance, with the former being criminal and the latter generally protected.

laws.title: Looting of Protected Archaeological Sites
laws.subtitle: Illegally excavating and stealing artifacts from heritage sites
laws.fullDescription: Kazakhstan criminal law treats the looting of protected archaeological sites — removing artifacts for sale on the black market — as a serious cultural heritage crime. Looted artifacts lose their scientific context and enrich criminal networks at the expense of national culture.
laws.penalty: 3 to 8 years imprisonment; mandatory restitution of artifacts
exceptions: Licensed archaeological fieldwork by accredited institutions
laws.sourceLabel: Kazakhstan Law on Culture — Archaeological Protection

quiz.q: What is lost when archaeological artifacts are looted rather than properly excavated?
options: Their scientific context and historical significance
quiz.explanation: Looted artifacts lose their archaeological context — the soil layers, associated finds, and spatial relationships that give them historical and scientific meaning.
